title: Introduce small-batch heuristic auditor and quant safety adapter
author: Arjun Patel
release_notes: Add a lightweight auditing tool that scans tenant prefill and batching defaults and emits safe quantization fallback rules. Includes a small CLI and telemetry events to integrate with Console alerts.
description: Motivation: Some tenants with low qps and narrow request distributions were picking aggressive default batch shapes and quant profiles that regressed latency and occasionally broke low-memory hosts. This PR adds a lightweight auditor and runtime adapter that (1) statically lints tenant prefill/batching defaults against observed shape histograms, (2) synthesizes conservative quantization safety fallbacks for affected tenants, and (3) surfaces deterministic telemetry so Console can create alerts and automated rollbacks. What changed: added a new CLI 'prefill-lint' under cmd/prefill-lint for offline checks; implemented runtime adapter in serving/prefill/safety_adapter.go that applies conservative quant/shape overrides when memory headroom is low; added a small telemetry bridge (observability/prefill_audit_bridge.go) that emits audit findings as events; extended the defaults manifest schema with an optional safety_profile block; unit/integration tests and docs. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4921) - [x] Unit tests for linter and adapter - [x] Integration smoke against a small local cluster - [x] Telemetry hooks added to Console-compatible channel - [x] Backwards compatible: new safety_profile is optional Rollout plan: Canary rollout on dedicated pools for 48h; observe telemetry and Console alerts; if we see >5% latency regression on pinned tenants revert adapter via feature flag. Related: SUP-879 incident postmortem influenced the heuristics in the linter. The description below lists commits, changed areas, review comments, CI summary, and merge details.
commits: add: initial prefill-lint CLI and linter engine
feat: runtime safety_adapter with conservative quant fallbacks
test: tests for linter heuristics and safety_adapter behavior
review_comments: Samantha Liu: Can you clarify the memory headroom threshold used by safety_adapter? Is it per-GPU or aggregate?
Arjun Patel: The threshold is per-device and derived from the device memory reporting plus a safety margin constant (see safety_adapter.go constants). I added comments and a short note in the docs.
Diego Morales: I ran the linter against the sample tenant set and found one false positive where very short sequences were flagged for prefill. Could we add a minimum seq-length guard?
Arjun Patel: Good catch. Added a min_sequence_length parameter and defaulted it to 8; test added to cover the short-sequence case.
Eve Chen: Telemetry schema looks fine. Please ensure events include deterministic tenant and sample keys for deduping in Console.
Arjun Patel: Telemetry now includes tenant_id, fingerprint, and heuristic_id. Observability bridge docs updated.
Samantha Liu: LGTM after addressing comments. Approving.
ci_checks: perf-smoke: flaky on first run -> rerun passed
e2e-console: pending (scheduled on next deploy, not blocking merge)
notes_on_risks: Conservative adapter is opt-in via defaults.safety_profile and guarded by per-tenant feature flags; risk limited to tenants with explicit safety profiles or those in canary. Rolling back is a one-line flag flip in feature flags service.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover linter heuristics and adapter fallback logic; integration smoke validates end-to-end behavior on a small cluster with synthetic workloads; manual perf smoke showed no regression for canary tenants; telemetry validated in staging Console.
how_to_revert: Revert by toggling the prefill-safety feature flag or revert the migration that introduces safety_profile in defaults schema. Ops runbook updated.
notes_for_oncall: Oncall should watch 'prefill.audit.finding' events and 'prefill.safety_applied' counters; a dashboard tile added under Prefill -> Safety. Alerts: >5% p50 latency increase or >0.5% error rate increase triggers immediate rollback.
changelog_entry: Add prefill-lint tool and runtime safety adapter to reduce accidental aggressive quant/batch defaults; introduce safety_profile in defaults schema (opt-in).
